heroes.name: Noah
heroes.lesson: When everyone laughed, Noah kept building because God asked him to. God kept His promise with a rainbow. Lesson: trust God even when others don’t.

heroes.name: Abraham
heroes.lesson: God promised Abraham children as many as the stars, and he believed. Lesson: God keeps His promises, even when we must wait.

heroes.name: Moses
heroes.lesson: Moses was shy about speaking, but God sent him to free His people from Egypt and gave him the Ten Commandments. Lesson: God gives strength for the job He asks.

heroes.name: Ruth
heroes.lesson: Ruth said to Naomi, “Where you go, I will go.” She became King David’s great-grandmother. Lesson: kindness to family matters to God.

heroes.name: David
heroes.lesson: A shepherd boy with five stones faced the giant Goliath, trusting God, not armour. Lesson: with God, small can beat big.

heroes.name: Esther
heroes.lesson: Queen Esther risked her life to save her people. “Perhaps you became queen for such a time as this.” Lesson: God puts you where you are for a reason.

heroes.name: Daniel
heroes.lesson: Daniel kept praying three times a day even when it was against the law. God shut the lions’ mouths. Lesson: never stop praying.

heroes.name: Jonah
heroes.lesson: Jonah ran away from God and ended up inside a great fish. God gave him another chance. Lesson: it’s never too late to say yes to God.

heroes.name: Mary
heroes.lesson: Mary said to the angel, “Let it be done to me according to your word.” Lesson: the greatest hero is the one who says yes to God.

heroes.name: Peter
heroes.lesson: Peter said three times he did not know Jesus, and Jesus forgave him three times. Jesus gave him the keys of the Kingdom. Lesson: Jesus always welcomes us back.

heroes.name: Paul
heroes.lesson: Paul hurt Christians until he met Jesus. Then he travelled the world telling everyone about Him. Lesson: anyone can change.

heroes.name: James
heroes.lesson: A fisherman whom Jesus called a “son of thunder”. Pilgrims still walk the Camino to honour him. Lesson: life is a journey with Jesus.

quizzes.title: Saint Riddles
quizzes.intro: Read the clues. Who am I?

questions.q: I cut my cloak in half to share with a freezing beggar. I was a Roman soldier.
I preached to birds and made peace with a wolf. I called the sun my brother.
I called my way to heaven the Little Way and promised a shower of roses.
I loved computers and built a website about Eucharistic miracles. I was canonized in 2025.
People ask me to help them find lost things. I was a great preacher from Portugal who lived in Italy.
I used a shamrock to teach about the Holy Trinity. Once I was a slave in the land I came back to save.
Mary appeared to me in a grotto. Later, many sick people came to the spring there.
I am the quiet carpenter who protected Jesus and Mary.
Roses filled my cloak, and Our Lady’s picture appeared on it in Mexico.
I secretly gave gifts to the poor. Children still put out shoes or stockings on my feast.
I was a doorkeeper in Montreal. People came to me for prayers, and I built a great oratory to St Joseph.
I wrote the Huron Carol, a Christmas song for the Wendat people of Canada.

questions.q: “Here I am! Send me.”
“Speak, Lord, for your servant is listening.”
“Let it be done to me according to your word.”
“My Lord and my God!”
“Where you go, I will go.”

catechism.a: God made me to know Him, love Him and serve Him in this world, and to be happy with Him for ever in the next.

catechism.q: To whose image and likeness did God make you?
catechism.a: God made me to His own image and likeness.

catechism.q: Is this likeness to God in your body, or in your soul?
catechism.a: This likeness to God is chiefly in my soul.

catechism.q: How is your soul like to God?
catechism.a: My soul is like to God because it is a spirit, and is immortal.

catechism.q: What do you mean when you say that your soul is immortal?
catechism.a: When I say that my soul is immortal, I mean that my soul can never die.

catechism.q: What must you do to save your soul?
catechism.a: To save my soul I must worship God by Faith, Hope and Charity; that is, I must believe in Him, I must hope in Him, and I must love Him with my whole heart.
Faith is a supernatural gift of God, which enables us to believe without doubting whatever God has revealed.

verses.text: Let the children come to me

Love one another as I have loved you
Your word is a lamp to my feet
With God all things are possible
I am the light of the world

This is the day the Lord has made

stories.title: David and the Giant
stories.summary: A shepherd boy, five smooth stones, and a very big problem.
body: Long ago, in the green hills of Bethlehem, a boy named David looked after his father’s sheep. He played songs on his harp, and when a lion or a bear came near, he chased it away. David was small, but he was not afraid, because he knew God was with him.

One day David brought bread to his big brothers in the army. Across the valley stood a giant named Goliath. He was taller than a doorway, with a bronze helmet and a spear like a tree trunk. “Send someone to fight me!” he roared. All the soldiers trembled.
“I will go,” said David. King Saul gave him armour, but it was so heavy David could barely walk. So he took it off. Instead he went to the stream and picked five smooth stones.
Goliath laughed. “Am I a dog, that you come at me with sticks?” David answered, “You come with a sword, but I come in the name of the Lord.”
David put one stone in his sling, swung it round and round, and let it fly. It struck Goliath on the forehead, and the giant fell flat on the ground!
David knew it wasn’t his strong arm that won. It was God. And when we have giant problems, we can trust God too.

stories.title: Francis and the Wolf
stories.summary: How St Francis made peace with a hungry wolf in the town of Gubbio.
body: In the town of Gubbio lived a very hungry wolf. He prowled outside the walls, and the people were so frightened they would not go out to their fields.

Brother Francis came to visit. He wore a rough brown robe tied with a rope, and he called the sun his brother and the moon his sister. “I will go and talk to Brother Wolf,” he said. The people gasped.

Francis walked out of the gate. The wolf ran at him with sharp teeth. Francis made the Sign of the Cross and said, gently, “Come here, Brother Wolf. In the name of Jesus, do not hurt anyone.” The wolf stopped. He lay down at Francis’s feet like a puppy.
“You have done wrong,” said Francis, “but you were hungry. If the people feed you every day, will you promise to make peace?” The wolf put his paw in Francis’s hand.
From that day the people fed the wolf, and he went from door to door like a friend. When he grew old and died, the whole town was sad.
Francis showed that kindness can be stronger than fear. Who is your “wolf”? Maybe someone who just needs a friend.

stories.title: Thérèse and the Little Way
stories.summary: A girl who wanted to be a great saint found an elevator to heaven.
body: Thérèse Martin was the youngest of five sisters in a happy home in France. Her papa called her his “little queen”. She wanted to become a great saint, but she felt too small.

“The great saints are like mountains,” she thought, “and I am like a grain of sand.” Then she had an idea. In fancy houses there were new machines called elevators that carried you up when you were too small to climb the stairs.
“Jesus will be my elevator!” she said. “I will just stay little and let Him lift me.” She called it her Little Way.
In the convent, Thérèse did small things with great love. She smiled at a sister who annoyed her. She didn’t complain when someone splashed dirty water on her. She did her chores as gifts for Jesus.
Thérèse died when she was only twenty-four, but she promised, “I will spend my heaven doing good on earth.” She said she would let fall a shower of roses, and many people say she still sends them.
You don’t have to be big to be a saint. Today, do one small thing with great love.

stories.title: Carlo’s Map of Miracles
stories.summary: A boy who loved computers used them to show the world Jesus.
body: Carlo Acutis was a boy from Milan in Italy who loved football, his dogs and cats, funny videos and video games. He was also very, very good with computers.
But Carlo’s favourite thing in the world was Jesus in the Eucharist. He went to Mass every day he could. “The Eucharist is my highway to heaven,” he said.
Carlo set himself a rule: only one hour of video games a week. He wanted to keep his heart free for God and for people.

Then he had an idea. He would use his computer skills to build a website about Eucharistic miracles from all over the world, so that everyone could learn how much Jesus loves us. It took him years, and people still visit it.
Carlo also made friends with the poor people in his neighbourhood, bringing them food and sleeping bags. He died of an illness when he was fifteen. In 2025 the Church declared him a saint.
Carlo said, “All people are born as originals, but many die as photocopies.” God made you an original too!

prayers.title: Sign of the Cross
prayers.text:
In the name of the Father,
and of the Son,
and of the Holy Spirit.
Amen.
prayers.tip: Touch your forehead, your heart, your left shoulder, then your right.

prayers.title: Our Father
prayers.text:
Our Father, who art in heaven,
hallowed be thy name;
thy kingdom come,
thy will be done
on earth as it is in heaven.
Give us this day our daily bread,
and forgive us our trespasses,
as we forgive those who trespass against us;
and lead us not into temptation,
but deliver us from evil.
Amen.
prayers.tip: Jesus taught this prayer to His friends (Matthew 6:9–13).

prayers.title: Hail Mary
prayers.text:
Hail Mary, full of grace,
the Lord is with thee.
Blessed art thou among women,
and blessed is the fruit of thy womb, Jesus.
Holy Mary, Mother of God,
pray for us sinners,
now and at the hour of our death.
Amen.
prayers.tip: The first lines are the words of the angel Gabriel and of Elizabeth (Luke 1).

prayers.title: Glory Be
prayers.text:
Glory be to the Father,
and to the Son,
and to the Holy Spirit,
as it was in the beginning,
is now, and ever shall be,
world without end.
Amen.
prayers.tip: A short prayer of praise to the Holy Trinity.

prayers.title: Guardian Angel
prayers.text:
Angel of God, my guardian dear,
to whom God’s love commits me here,
ever this day be at my side,
to light and guard, to rule and guide.
Amen.
prayers.tip: A perfect prayer for the morning or before bed.

prayers.title: Grace Before Meals
prayers.text:
Bless us, O Lord,
and these thy gifts,
which we are about to receive
from thy bounty,
through Christ our Lord.
Amen.
prayers.tip: Say it together as a family before you eat.

prayers.title: Morning Offering
prayers.text:
O Jesus, through the Immaculate Heart of Mary,
I offer you my prayers, works, joys and sufferings of this day
for all the intentions of your Sacred Heart.
Amen.
prayers.tip: A short form of the traditional Morning Offering. Give your whole day to Jesus.

prayers.title: Act of Contrition
prayers.text:
My God, I am sorry for my sins with all my heart.
In choosing to do wrong and failing to do good,
I have sinned against you whom I should love above all things.
I firmly intend, with your help, to do penance,
to sin no more, and to avoid whatever leads me to sin.
Our Saviour Jesus Christ suffered and died for us.
In his name, my God, have mercy.
Amen.
prayers.tip: Prayed in Confession, and at night before sleep.
